q: List the 4 levels of management in PRINCE2.
a: Project commissioning (business layer) → Orientation (project board) → Management (project manager) → Delivery (team managers).

q: Who constitutes the Project Board?
a: Executive, Senior User (Senior User), Senior Supplier (Senior Supplier).

q: Who is ultimately responsible for the project's success?
a: project executive (Executive).

q: What functions cannot be performed by the Project Manager?
a: He cannot be a member of the Project Board (including the Executive) or perform Project Assurance.

q: What does Project Assurance do?
a: Independent monitoring of work on behalf of the Project Board (business, users, suppliers).

q: What does Project Support do?
a: Administration, record keeping and PM tool support.

q: What is the name of the role responsible for delivering the Work Package?
a: Team Manager.

q: Can the Project Board have only one member?
a: Yes, if the Executive also takes on the roles of Senior User and Senior Supplier.

q: What is the goal of the Organization practice?
a: The purpose of the Organization practice is to define and establish a project accountability and responsibility structure (who).

q: What is the business layer preparing?
a: Commissioning the project to complete it with an outline that the project board agrees to.

q: Who appoints the Executive and can his or her accountability be delegated?
a: It is determined by business. It is a single point of accountability for the project; this accountability CANNOT be delegated.

q: What approach is the Senior User accountable for?
a: For the approach to capturing user requirements and benefit specifications aligned with the business case.

q: What two areas is the Senior Supplier responsible for?
a: For the quality of products delivered by suppliers and the technical integrity of the project.

q: List the 7 management areas of a project manager.
a: Benefits, costs, time, risk, quality, scope, sustainability.

q: On whose behalf does the Project Manager act and within what limits?
a: On behalf of the Project Board, within agreed tolerances and limits.

q: How does the PM assign work to the Team Manager?
a: In the form of a description of the Work Package, in accordance with the Commercial Management Approach.

q: Does securing arrangements only apply to formal contracts?
a: NO. PM secures ALL arrangements: formal contracts with external suppliers and informal arrangements with colleagues, such as when and how changes are made.

q: Who MUST NOT be entrusted with Project Assurance?
a: The project manager, team members or project support.

q: Does appointing people to Project Oversight transfer the accountability of the Board?
a: NO. Board members remain accountable for the oversight of their areas.

q: Who is responsible for Project Support by default?
a: Project Manager. Can delegate this responsibility; Project support can be established as a project office.

q: What needs does Business represent?
a: Meeting business needs and providing value for money. Representative: Executive.

q: Who is covered by the User side of interest?
a: People who use, operate, maintain or support the results, and those who are affected by the results. Representative: Senior User.

q: What does the Supplier's side of interest bring?
a: Resources with specific skills needed to produce products. Representative: Senior Supplier.

q: What work limits apply to the Team Manager?
a: Agreed specifications and tolerances agreed with the Project Manager.
